2.text: In the olden times, as I was told, a company of young men would seize

3.text: a young girl in the open, bind her hands and feet, and carry her to the

4.text: house of one who wanted to have her for a wife. Not only the men of alien

5.text: families, but even the relatives and the cousins, acted so, after having been

6.text: refused by the father of the girl. The assault and the ravishing, however,

7.text: were not considered as a reason for implacable hatred and feuds. The parents

8.text: would come afterward and ask for ransom, which was paid, not in reindeer,

10.text: If the parents gave pursuit on the fresh track, the ravisher would make

11.text: haste, first of all, to perform the marriage ritual with the ravished girl, anointing

12.text: her, if not with the blood of sacrifice, at least with some soot and coal-powder

13.text: from the family hearth. At the same time he would bid one of the women

14.text: of his family get ready to go away as ransom. In this way, bloodshed might

15.text: have been avoided, even after the meeting of both hostile parties.

16.text: Even at present a case of ravishment may happen now and then. Thus,

28.text: Marriage by Flight. — More frequent than the ravishing of women,
28.note: third-level run-in heading, italic title case as printed (§2.13); em dash U+2014 (§2.11)

29.text: in modern times, is marriage by flight.

30.text: I should mention that the element of constraint on the part of the parents

31.text: as to the choice of the bridegroom exists among the Chukchee, as almost

32.text: everywhere. It even happens, and is in accord with the national character,

33.text: that the bride prefers to take her own life rather than be married against her

34.text: will. At the same time there are cases of love-marriages contrary to the will

36.text: Those cases of which I know, however, happened in weak, disintegrated

37.text: families. A strong family would resent an outrage like this, and strive to

38.text: take the woman back, unless paid ransom in the same specie. Thus to

39.text: my knowledge, in the country on the Dry Anui River, one girl left her camp

40.text: and family, and fled to a travelling-camp of one of the Maritime traders.

41.text: The man was already in middle life and had two other wives; but he was

42.text: strong, healthy, and daring, the actual type of a travelling Chukchee adven-
